title: Transport service in a named terminal, with a one-turn clarification
passenger_input: "Where does the long-stay car park shuttle leave from at Terminal 1?" — then the quick reply Car Park P1
expected_behaviour: A KB-grounded answer for the Terminal 1 parking record; a clarification is acceptable if the wording matches more than one transport record within the margin rule
actual_system_behaviour: Turn 1: "There are 2 transport locations in Terminal 1: Car Park P1 or Terminal Shuttle (T1 ↔ T2). Which one do you mean?" — Question back to you, From your words. Turn 2: "Car Park P1 is in Terminal 1, P1 (Opposite Terminal 1; footbridge at Level 1). From Departures, cross the covered footbridge at the north end of the Check-in Hall." Location · Hours: always open · Access: step-free; Strong match; evidence Why = "A place name in your question"
observed_limitation: "Long-stay car park shuttle" did not separate a shuttle to a car park from the shuttle between terminals in the KB descriptions, so the system asked rather than answered directly; two turns were needed
suggested_improvement: Add discriminating aliases (e.g. "long-stay", "P1 shuttle") to the parking record, or show one-line descriptions with the clarification options so the passenger can choose faster

title: Photographed sign without any words
passenger_input: `img_007.png` (AIGA information pictogram, development split; not in any blind set), text box empty
expected_behaviour: Recognise the sign category and, because information desks exist in both terminals, ask which terminal rather than guess
actual_system_behaviour: "This looks like an information sign. Are you in Terminal 1 or Terminal 2?" — Question back to you, From your photo; evidence: category information 0.31 (cosine), options = Flight Information boards, Information Desk T2, Information Desk T1 Arrivals, Information Desk T1 Departures; quick replies Terminal 1 / Terminal 2
observed_limitation: With no words and no terminal, the image alone cannot resolve to one of four information records; the flight-information boards are listed among the options although a "?" pictogram usually denotes a staffed desk
suggested_improvement: Weight the information-desk records above the flight-information boards for the information pictogram, or ask "desk or departure boards?" after the terminal is known

title: Spoken question about ground transport at the other terminal
passenger_input: Synthetic 16 kHz clip, "Where can I catch a taxi outside Terminal 2?"
expected_behaviour: Transcript shown for correction; answer the taxi record and make clear which terminal it is in
actual_system_behaviour: Heard as "Where can I catch a taxi outside Terminal 2?" (verbatim); answer "Taxi Rank also serves Terminal 2. Taxi Rank is in Terminal 1, Forecourt (Arrivals, Level 0 (outside)). Exit the Arrivals Hall and turn right along the forecourt." Hours: staffed marshal 06:00–23:00, taxis at all times; Strong match; From your voice; editable transcript displayed
observed_limitation: The directions are written from the Terminal 1 Arrivals Hall; a passenger standing in Terminal 2 gets the right record but not a route from where they are. The clip was synthesised and uploaded, not recorded through the microphone
suggested_improvement: Store terminal-relative directions for records that serve both terminals; complete a live-microphone check before submission (see below)

title: Photographed sign plus a deictic question naming the terminal
passenger_input: `img_007.png` + "I'm in Terminal 1, where is the nearest one of these?"
expected_behaviour: Image supplies the category, text supplies the terminal; candidates narrowed to Terminal 1 information records, then either an answer or a clarification among them
actual_system_behaviour: "This looks like an information sign. Which one do you mean: Flight Information (Departure and Arrival Boards), Information Desk, Terminal 1 Arrivals or Information Desk, Terminal 1 Departures?" — Question back to you, "From your photo, words used to narrow down"; technical details: entities `terminal = Terminal 1`, `deictic_ref = these`; text intent scored weak (`find_transport` 0.60), image led; candidates correctly limited to the three Terminal 1 records; flags `text weak, image needs terminal`
correct: Safe clarification; routing correct, explanation partly inconsistent
observed_limitation: The candidate list was narrowed to Terminal 1, yet an evidence line still reads "terminal unknown" and the quick reply offers "Terminal 1" again; "nearest" cannot be used because the passenger's position within the terminal is unknown
suggested_improvement: Generate the evidence wording and quick replies from the narrowed candidate set rather than from the image-only branch; when the terminal is known, offer the remaining records as the quick replies

title: Service the airport does not have, phrased as a purchase
passenger_input: "Is there a post office where I can buy stamps in the airport?"
expected_behaviour: No KB answer; abstain with a reason that says the service is not covered, and do not invent a location
actual_system_behaviour: "I cannot book, reserve, print or arrange anything; I can only give information about the airport." — No reliable match; evidence Outcome = No answer, retrieval stage `no_retrieval`; technical details: entities `unsupported_service = post office`, flags `unsupported_service, action_request`, why = "'post office' is a service the knowledge base does not hold"
correct: Safe abstention; reason wording less precise than the evidence
observed_limitation: Both `unsupported_service` and `action_request` fired ("buy" matched the action rule); the passenger-facing sentence chose the action-request wording, while the accurate reason appears only under Technical details
suggested_improvement: Rank the unsupported-service explanation above the action-request explanation whenever a named unsupported service is present; consider pointing to the information desk as the official source for services outside the KB
